requirement_text.ISS-0878: Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipelineTest's unique_realm/1 uses a per-BEAM-process monotonic counter, so two parallel test_parallel.sh partitions can independently generate the same idp_realm_id and collide on tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index. Found during TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 full-suite verification for WF02-REQ421-20260928 (scripts/test_parallel.sh, N=16 nproc-derived, combined 5028 tests / 6 properties / 3 failures, 5031/5034 passed). git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD for that branch confirmed test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs is NOT touched (that branch's diff is limited to apps/mobile/, docs/mobile/, and doc-bookkeeping files), so this failure is pre-existing, not a regression from that branch. Partition 3 failed: 'acceptance criterion 4 -- realm-ownership guard rejects mismatch, no JIT under wrong tenant / the realm-ownership guard rejects a tenant that does not own the token's claimed realm...' (test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs:220) with: ** (Ecto.InvalidChangesetError) could not perform insert because changeset is invalid. Errors: %{idp_realm_id: [{"has already been taken", [constraint: :unique, constraint_name: "tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index"]}]}. Applied changes: %{..., idp_realm_id: "owned-by-a-1"}. Root-cause mechanism (code inspection, not yet reproduced in isolation): auth_pipeline_test.exs:64-66 defines its own unique_realm(prefix) -> "#{prefix}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic])}". System.unique_integer/1 is unique only WITHIN one BEAM VM process -- its monotonic counter restarts from 1 in every fresh VM. scripts/test_parallel.sh shards the suite across N independent mix test --partitions N OS processes (separate BEAM VMs), all against the same shared Postgres instance (tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index is a single, global partial unique index, not partition-scoped). Two different partitions each calling unique_realm("owned-by-a") as the FIRST such call in their own process both produce the literal string "owned-by-a-1" -- an exact collision on the global unique index once both partitions attempt the insert. This is the same general class already diagnosed for retention_operations_test.exs (ISS-0873: cross-partition TOCTOU race on unscoped global reads/writes under test_parallel.sh) and the same specific mechanism ISS-0329 fixed a FIXED-STRING realm collision for elsewhere in this file's own module (ISS-0329's fix note: 'Closing the fixed-realm window means two concurrent partitions can no longer collide on idp_realm_id' -- ISS-0329 assumed unique_realm/1, once introduced, was collision-proof across partitions; this finding shows it is not, because System.unique_integer/1 is only process-local unique, not globally unique). NOT the same symptom as any currently-open issue: searched docs/issues/ for 'idp_realm_id', 'tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index', 'AuthPipelineTest', 'auth_pipeline_test' -- no exact match found. Severity MINOR -- only reproduces under full parallel-suite contention (same class as ISS-0873), requires two different partitions to independently make their FIRST unique_realm(prefix) call with the same prefix in the same narrow window, and has not been observed to reproduce twice in a row. No evidence of a production defect; this is purely a test-fixture collision-avoidance gap. fix_direction (as filed, NOT INVESTIGATED beyond code-inspection root cause): replace or supplement System.unique_integer/1 in unique_realm/1 (this file, and any other test file using the same process-local-only pattern) with a source that is unique across separate OS processes -- e.g. mix the OS process id (System.pid/0) or :erlang.unique_integer/0 combined with a partition identifier (System.get_env("MIX_TEST_PARTITION")) into the generated string, or switch to a UUID/random-suffix scheme. TEST-DESIGNER should audit whether other test files share this exact unique_realm/1 definition (grep showed at least test/letflow/api/authorization_ac9_test.exs:49 and test/letflow/oidc/provider_registry_multi_realm_test.exs:83 use the identical pattern) versus the collision-proof helper already established in test/letflow/identity_test.exs -- consolidating onto one shared, genuinely-cross-process-unique helper (same spirit as ISS-0112's TenantFixture consolidation) would close this for all call sites at once rather than one file at a time. Affected files: test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs, test/letflow/api/authorization_ac9_test.exs, test/letflow/oidc/provider_registry_multi_realm_test.exs.

source_text.test/letflow/identity_test.exs:
defp unique_realm(prefix \\ "realm") do
  "#{prefix}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic])}"
end

defp unique_slug(prefix \\ "tenant") do
  Letflow.TenantSlugFixture.unique_slug(prefix)
end
source_text.test/support/tenant_slug.ex:
defmodule Letflow.TenantSlugFixture do
  @moduledoc """
  Shared, collision-proof `tenants.slug` fixture generator ... Fixes ISS-0059: System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic]) is only unique within a single BEAM VM run ... Ecto.UUID.generate/0 is not derived from any in-process counter or wall-clock value that resets, so a slug built from it is collision-proof across VM restarts as well as within a single run.
  """
  @spec unique_slug(prefix :: String.t()) :: String.t()
  def unique_slug(prefix) when is_binary(prefix) do
    "#{prefix}-#{Ecto.UUID.generate()}"
  end
end

task.description: Design a fix for ISS-0878. Read this handoff's result.summary in full for the confirmed root cause and the concrete fix shape before designing anything.
acceptance_criteria: Design introduces (or specifies extending an existing test/support module with) a collision-proof realm-id generator that is unique across separate OS processes, not just within one BEAM VM -- e.g. following test/support/tenant_slug.ex's Ecto.UUID.generate()-based precedent.

Design covers all 3 affected call sites (test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs, test/letflow/api/authorization_ac9_test.exs, test/letflow/oidc/provider_registry_multi_realm_test.exs), replacing each file's own private unique_realm/1 with a call to the shared helper.

Design states explicitly whether test/letflow/identity_test.exs's own unique_realm/1 (same vulnerable System.unique_integer/1 pattern, confirmed still present) is in scope for this fix or deliberately deferred -- do not silently leave it unaddressed without a stated reason.
Design does not alter any assertion semantics in the 3 (or 4) files -- this is a fixture-generation fix only, no behavioral test changes.
Design is test-only (test/ and test/support/ paths only); no lib/ or priv/repo/migrations/ changes are implicated by this issue.

result.summary: STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): grepped docs/issues/ for idp_realm_id / unique_realm / AuthPipelineTest / partition collision -- 12 files matched, none a resolved entry for this exact symptom (ISS-0329 fixed a *different*, earlier bug in the same file -- a FIXED-STRING realm literal colliding across partitions -- and its own fix note explicitly assumed unique_realm/1, once introduced afterward, would be collision-proof; that assumption is what this issue disproves). ISS-0873 is the same general class (cross-partition contention under scripts/test_parallel.sh) but a different specific mechanism (TOCTOU on unscoped reads/writes, not a generator collision) in a different file. Checked whether ISS-0112's TenantFixture consolidation (batch 4b, commit f4185e8e, merged 2026-09-28) already touched these files: it did -- auth_pipeline_test.exs and authorization_ac9_test.exs were both migrated from their hand-rolled Sandbox/insert_tenant!/provision_tenant_schema/on_exit boilerplate onto Letflow.TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 (with an idp_realm_id opt added in cd2cfd41/PR #1933 specifically to support these two files' realm-threading need). CRITICALLY, this consolidation did NOT touch the realm-STRING-GENERATION helper at all -- TenantFixture.provisioned_tenant!/1 (test/support/tenant_fixture.ex:235-252) accepts an idp_realm_id string as an opt and threads it through verbatim; it has no logic that generates one. Each of the 3 affected files still defines and calls its own private unique_realm/1 to produce that string, unchanged by the ISS-0112 migration -- confirmed by reading current tree: auth_pipeline_test.exs:64-66, authorization_ac9_test.exs:49, provider_registry_multi_realm_test.exs:83 all still read `defp unique_realm(prefix) [, do:] "#{prefix}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic])}"` verbatim. So this is confirmed NOT already fixed by ISS-0112; it is a live, distinct gap in a helper ISS-0112 deliberately left alone. STEP 1 (diagnose): could not force a genuine cross-partition collision on demand in this session -- it requires two separate `mix test --partitions N` OS processes each making unique_realm("owned-by-a") as their literal first call in the same narrow window, which is inherently timing-dependent and not something a single diagnostic run can reliably trigger; stating this explicitly rather than claiming a reproduction that didn't happen. Root-cause mechanism CONFIRMED by direct code reading (not just inherited from the issue's prose): System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic]) is documented (and empirically established by this repo's own ISS-0059 fix, see below) to be a per-BEAM-VM-process monotonic counter that restarts at a low value in every fresh VM -- it carries no cross-process uniqueness guarantee whatsoever. scripts/test_parallel.sh shards test execution across N independent OS processes/BEAM VMs hitting one shared Postgres instance; tenants_idp_realm_id_partial_index is a single global unique index with no partition scoping. Two partitions independently calling unique_realm("owned-by-a") as their first invocation of that prefix in their own process both produce the identical string "owned-by-a-1", and the second partition's insert attempt raises Ecto.InvalidChangesetError on the unique constraint -- exactly the observed failure. EXISTING PRECEDENT FOR THE FIX, found by reading test/support/tenant_slug.ex directly: Letflow.TenantSlugFixture.unique_slug/1 (test/support/tenant_slug.ex:1-24) was built for the EXACT SAME failure class one level up the stack -- ISS-0059 ('System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic]) is only unique within a single BEAM VM run... a slug built from it is collision-proof across VM restarts as well as within a single run' -- quoted verbatim from that module's own moduledoc) -- and its fix is to build the string from Ecto.UUID.generate() instead of System.unique_integer/1, since a UUID carries no in-process-counter or wall-clock dependency. identity_test.exs itself independently reaches the same conclusion in its own inline comment at line 872-877 ('Ecto.UUID.generate/0-derived, NOT System.unique_integer/1 -- the latter is only unique within a single BEAM VM run...') when justifying its unique_hostname/1 helper. HOWEVER -- IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THIS RUN'S OWN BRIEFING: the task context asserted identity_test.exs 'already has a collision-proof helper' for realm generation that the 3 affected files could simply adopt. That is FALSE, verified by reading identity_test.exs:80-81 directly: its own unique_realm/1 is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the 3 affected files' vulnerable pattern (`"#{prefix}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic])}"`) -- identity_test.exs has the SAME bug, not a fix for it. What identity_test.exs actually has that IS collision-proof is unique_slug/1 (a thin wrapper delegating to Letflow.TenantSlugFixture.unique_slug/1) and, separately, its own private unique_hostname/1 -- neither of which is a realm-id generator. There is currently NO existing shared, cross-process-unique realm-id helper anywhere in the codebase; TenantSlugFixture only covers slugs. WHAT A FIX MUST CHANGE, concretely: (1) add a new function -- either exported from test/support/tenant_slug.ex (e.g. Letflow.TenantSlugFixture.unique_realm/1) or a new small test/support module -- that generates a realm-id string via Ecto.UUID.generate() (or an equivalent cross-process-unique source; NOT System.unique_integer/1 in any arity), following the exact precedent test/support/tenant_slug.ex:20-23 already establishes for slugs; (2) replace the private unique_realm/1 definitions at test/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline_test.exs:64-66, test/letflow/api/authorization_ac9_test.exs:49, and test/letflow/oidc/provider_registry_multi_realm_test.exs:83 with calls to that shared helper, removing the now-dead private defp in each file; (3) explicitly decide (and design doc should state which) whether test/letflow/identity_test.exs:80-81's own unique_realm/1 -- confirmed to share the identical vulnerable pattern, found by this diagnosis but outside ISS-0878's originally-filed 3-file affected_files list -- is folded into this same fix (consolidating a 4th call site) or filed as its own follow-up issue; leaving it silently unfixed after finding it would repeat exactly the kind of partial-fix gap ISS-0329 itself left behind. No lib/ or priv/repo/migrations/ changes are implicated -- this is a test-fixture-only defect. Why existing tests didn't catch it: the collision is inherently a race between independent OS processes under scripts/test_parallel.sh's real sharding, not reproducible by any single-process `mix test` run, so no unit test on unique_realm/1 itself would ever exercise the failure mode; it can only be caught statistically, by noticing failures across many parallel full-suite runs, exactly how TEST-RUNNER found it.

issues.description: This run's own dispatching briefing asserted test/letflow/identity_test.exs 'already has a collision-proof helper' for realm generation that the 3 affected files could adopt. Verified false by reading the file directly: identity_test.exs:80-81's unique_realm/1 is byte-identical to the vulnerable pattern in the 3 affected files (same System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic]) construction) -- it is a 4th instance of the same bug, not a fix for it. The genuinely collision-proof precedent in this codebase is test/support/tenant_slug.ex's Letflow.TenantSlugFixture.unique_slug/1 (UUID-based), which covers slugs, not realm ids. Flagging per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 1.1 (a handoff's factual premises are checkable) so CODE-DESIGNER does not inherit the false premise, and so identity_test.exs's exposure gets a deliberate scope decision rather than silent omission.
